tagline: Stockholm built on fourteen islands — the archipelago capital where the commute already wants to be on the water.
summary: Sweden's marine-mobility heart is Stockholm, a capital built across fourteen islands at the mouth of Lake Mälaren, opening into a vast Baltic archipelago of thousands of islands. The city already runs commuter and leisure ferries to Djurgården, Vaxholm and the archipelago, and is the home of Candela, whose electric hydrofoils are entering scheduled service here. It is the world's proving ground for foiling public transport — and a dense, affluent, water-defined market for a clean fast tier.
why_marine_mobility: Stockholm is the definitive archipelago commute: islands minutes apart by water but long loops by bridge and road. Navier's Pioneer II flies the inner-city and near-archipelago mesh — the Djurgården hop, the Nacka and Ekerö commuter runs, the Vaxholm and Sandhamn archipelago legs — silent, dry and zero-emission, while the Quanta-LR opens the longer Baltic trunks to Mariehamn and across to Helsinki.

demand_signals.label: Stockholm commuter-ferry network
demand_signals.note: The city already runs high-volume commuter boats (SL/Waxholmsbolaget) across its island core and out to the archipelago — proven dense daily water demand.

demand_signals.label: Stockholm archipelago
demand_signals.note: Thousands of islands — Vaxholm, Sandhamn, Grinda — draw very heavy summer leisure and second-home traffic on slow conventional ferries.

demand_signals.label: Candela foiling proof-point
demand_signals.note: Candela's electric hydrofoils entering scheduled Stockholm public transport validate clean foiling craft in exactly this commute, on the home water.

use_cases.body: A clean foiling commuter tier across Stockholm's island core — Djurgården, Nacka Strand, Ekerö — and out to Vaxholm, replacing slow diesel ferries with fast, dry hops.
Fast archipelago leisure runs to Sandhamn, Grinda and the outer islands that compress hours of conventional-ferry time.
Premium Baltic line-haul to Mariehamn and across to Helsinki on the Quanta-LR as range comes online.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The city-and-near-archipelago mesh — Slussen↔Djurgården (~0.5 nm), Nybroplan↔Nacka Strand (~3 nm), Klara Mälarstrand↔Ekerö (~8.6 nm), Stockholm↔Vaxholm (~12 nm), Strandvägen↔Sandhamn (~26 nm) — sits inside the 70 nm all-electric range off existing quays.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The inner network is pure Pioneer II territory; longer Baltic trunks — Stockholm↔Mariehamn (~75 nm), Stockholm↔Helsinki (~210 nm) — are Quanta-LR hybrid corridors (H2 2026+) with no mid-sea charging dependency.

transit_planning: For SL/Waxholmsbolaget or the Region Stockholm transport authority: a clean fast tier slotting into a mature commuter-ferry network, on the same home water where foiling public transport is already being proven.
competitive_landscape: Stockholm has an established but largely diesel commuter and archipelago ferry fleet; Candela's electric hydrofoils are the first foiling entrant. The opportunity is a fast, dry, zero-emission tier across the island core and archipelago, in the most foiling-receptive market in the world.
regulatory_note: Water transport falls under Region Stockholm (SL) and Waxholmsbolaget, with the Swedish Transport Agency (Transportstyrelsen) as maritime regulator. Sweden's clean grid, climate policy and the precedent of foiling craft already in scheduled service make this an unusually supportive regulatory and public environment.
seasonality: A strong summer peak (May–September) for archipelago and leisure traffic with long Nordic daylight; the inner-city commuter runs year-round. Winter Baltic ice in the outer archipelago concentrates long-leg service on the open-water season, where foiling's smooth ride suits the choppy crossings.
